cases.setup: Provide a public Python analyzer checkout with an assignment-expression target incorrectly stored in a comprehension-local scope.
checks: The recorded TaskContext identifies current classifier, inserter, comprehension-scope model, and test owners with code anchors.
The trace records the actual target insertion destination and the containing non-comprehension scope.
Public generator and nested-comprehension diagnostic results are recorded without changing checkout files.
A successful diagnosis PortValue is emitted only when observations confirm the defect.

cases.setup: Supply a confirmed diagnosis and bound owners in a Python analyzer using consecutive comprehension scopes.
checks: The diff distinguishes assignment-expression bindings from ordinary assignments.
Only assignment-expression bindings bypass consecutive comprehension scopes and insertion stops at the first non-comprehension scope.
Existing annotation treatment and syntax guards remain intact.
Public single-generator and nested-comprehension regression assertions are present.
The output is marked modified-unvalidated and previous diagnostic results are invalidated.

cases.setup: Provide a repaired checkout with regression assertions and current public Oracle command bindings.
checks: Executed public commands, exit statuses, and diagnostics are recorded.
The single-generator target y receives no undefined-name diagnostic.
Nested-comprehension targets y and z receive no undefined-name diagnostics.
Adjacent public checks confirm ordinary assignment behavior, annotation behavior, iteration-variable locality, and containing-scope boundaries.
Failures or unavailable checks are reported as FAIL or UNKNOWN rather than PASS.
Reported validation scope distinguishes focused test results from whole-project coverage.
